title: The Works of Philo Judaeus, Vol. 1
author: Philo of Alexandria (Yonge trans)
description: The Works of Philo Judaeus, the contemporary of Josephus, Volume 1, translated from the Greek by C. D. Yonge (London: Henry G. Bohn, 1854), in Bohn's Ecclesiastical Library. Philo of Alexandria (c. 20 BCE-50 CE), the Hellenistic Jewish philosopher, sought to harmonise the Torah with Greek philosophy, especially Platonism and Stoicism, through allegorical interpretation. This first volume of Yonge's four-volume translation includes On the Creation of the World, the Allegorical Interpretation of Genesis, On the Cherubim, On the Sacrifices of Abel and Cain, That the Worse Is Wont to Attack the Better, On the Posterity of Cain, On the Giants and On the Unchangeableness of God, among others. Philo's doctrine of the Logos as God's instrument of creation, the heavenly and earthly man, and the soul's ascent influenced the Gospel of John, the Church Fathers, Gnosticism and Kabbalah.
